modules.title: How to look
modules.purpose: The practical skills every observer uses: getting your eyes ready, finding directions, and measuring the sky with your hand.
objectives: Prepare your eyes for the dark and protect your night vision
Find north, south, east and west from the sky itself
Measure distances in the sky with your hand at arm's length
Describe any position by altitude and direction, and read star brightness in magnitudes
Judge how much light pollution hides at your site

modules.title: How the sky moves
modules.purpose: Why the stars turn through the night, change with the seasons, and depend on where on Earth you stand.
objectives: Explain the nightly rotation of the sky around the celestial pole
Tell which stars never set, which never rise, and which rise and set at your latitude
Predict how the evening sky shifts from month to month
Use the altitude of the celestial pole to work out your latitude

modules.title: Finding your way
modules.purpose: Star-hopping: using patterns you know to find the ones you don't. Learn the three methods, then the ten classic hops.
objectives: Use lines, arcs and triangles between bright stars to find new ones
Perform the ten most widely taught star-hops from memory
Use a seasonal signpost as a starting point for that part of the sky

modules.title: Your first constellations
modules.purpose: The fifteen brightest, most recognizable constellations visible from your location: the framework you hang everything else on.
objectives: Find each anchor constellation in the real sky
Name its brightest stars and say when in the year it is best placed
Retell at least one story for each

modules.title: Season by season
modules.purpose: Every other constellation you can see from your location, grouped by the evenings when it is best placed.
objectives: Find the remaining constellations visible from your location, starting from the anchors
Know which months each group is best seen in the evening
Recognize the stories and notable objects in each group

modules.title: Sun, Moon and planets
modules.purpose: The bodies that move against the stars: why they follow the ecliptic, how they move, and the events they create.
objectives: Explain the ecliptic and why the Sun, Moon and planets stay near it
Tell a planet from a star and predict when each planet is well placed
Explain retrograde motion, the Moon's phases and eclipses
Plan an evening around a meteor shower

modules.title: What's out there
modules.purpose: What the points and smudges really are: stars of every kind, nebulae, clusters, galaxies and planets up close.
objectives: Read a star's temperature from its colour and place it in its life story
Tell the main kinds of nebula, cluster and galaxy apart
Choose good targets for your eyes, binoculars or a small telescope

modules.title: Beyond your horizon
modules.purpose: The constellations that never rise from your location — for travel, or to complete all 88.
objectives: Recognize the constellations of the other hemisphere
Know how far you would need to travel to see each one
